newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Death toll rises to 32 in Pakistan gas leak.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to 32 in Pakistan gas leak.

text.p: The death toll from a toxic gas leak in the Pakistani city of Lahore rose to 32 on Friday after two more people died in hospital, doctors said.

They said 90 people were still in hospital, of whom 18 were in critical condition. More than 900 people were treated in hospitals after the gas leak in the populous Mughalpura district of the Punjab provincial capital on Wednesday night.
The pungent smell of the gas, now identified by officials as chlorine rather than ammonia as first thought, still hung over the area and experts said it could take a week to disperse.
The impoverished district, home to many railway employees, was plunged into mourning, with families burying their dead and the wails of women echoing through the narrow streets.
On Thursday night relatives buried five members of a single family in which only a baby had survived.
Other residents recounted the panic that swept the area when liquid gas spilled from cylinders on a truck that had broken down. Police said the driver was still at large.

"We were at home on Wednesday night with our three daughters and son," Noor Jahan told the Urdu-language Khabrain newspaper. "When the gas leaked, we rushed out of the house, but one of our daughters was left behind."
She said her husband Boota had gone back to rescue her, but fell unconscious and later died in hospital.
Another woman, named only as Kausar, ran out of her house with her two children, who then fainted. Unable to carry them, she also succumbed and died in hospital. The children survived.
Many buffaloes kept by residents for milk choked to death after the accident. Troops and workers with cranes and trucks removed the decaying, bloated carcasses on Thursday.
Humayun Arshad, a doctor treating the casualties, said he believed the gas could cause blindness and mental disorders.
Police have filed a case against unknown persons, having failed to trace those responsible for the accident involving the cylinders, said to have been on their way to a jeans factory.
